answer: An agent economy can make fake identities expensive by requiring each new agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a deposit on an island ferry ticket: the stake is trivial for one honest agent but ruinous across ten thousand clones. The horizon for profit then shrinks, because any Sybil caught cheating forfeits its bond. Like karst caves that form only over centuries, reputation accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, so a flood of fresh identities starts with zero trust and zero leverage, while established agents keep their hard-earned standing.
